# Flexible Array Members Done Right

## Thesis

A **flexible array member** (C99) is the standard way to attach a variable-length payload to a struct without a second allocation. `sizeof` the struct excludes the payload; you allocate `sizeof(header) + n` bytes and treat `data[]` as the tail.

## Mental model

```text
  malloc(sizeof(struct packet) + n)
  ┌──────────┬─────────────────────┐
  │ len      │ data[0 .. n-1]      │
  └──────────┴─────────────────────┘
       ↑ sizeof(struct packet) stops here
```

Rules of thumb:

- The FAM must be the **last** member.
- Do not declare arrays of the struct type.
- Prefer `sizeof *p + n` over guessing padding.

## Worked example

Verified with **GCC 14.2**, `-std=c11 -Wall`.

```c
/* fam.c */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdint.h>

struct packet {
  uint16_t len;
  char data[];          /* flexible array member */
};

int main(void) {
  size_t n = 5;
  struct packet *p = malloc(sizeof *p + n);
  if (!p) return 1;
  p->len = (uint16_t)n;
  memcpy(p->data, "hello", n);
  printf("sizeof(struct packet)=%zu payload=%.*s len=%u\n",
         sizeof(struct packet), (int)p->len, p->data, p->len);
  free(p);
  return 0;
}
```

```bash
gcc -O2 -std=c11 -Wall fam.c -o fam && ./fam
```

```text
sizeof(struct packet)=2 payload=hello len=5
```

`sizeof(struct packet)` is just the fixed header (here 2 bytes, possibly padded). The five payload bytes live past that.

## Trap

**`struct packet p; p.data[0] = 'x';` on a stack instance.** There is no storage for `data`. Same for `struct packet arr[10];`. Also avoid the pre-C99 GCC `[0]` hack in new code — use `[]`.

## Boring rule

One allocation: `malloc(sizeof *hdr + payload_bytes)`. Check overflow of the size addition before calling `malloc`. Free the single pointer.

## Try this

1. Add a `uint32_t checksum` before `data[]` and re-check `sizeof`.
2. Pass `-Wflexible-array-extensions` / pedantic flags and clean warnings.
3. Compare with a pointer-to-heap design (`char *data`) and count syscalls under `strace` (when available).

## Sources

- ISO/IEC 9899:1999 §6.7.2.1 (flexible array members)
